passages.text: Woe to you, O Ariel, the city of Ariel where David camped! Year upon year let your festivals recur.
passages.sermon:
Ariel is a city.
David camped in Ariel.
Ariel is called the city of Ariel.
Woe comes to Ariel.
Your festivals will happen again and again.
Each year, your festivals will return.
passages.original: ה֚וֹי אֲרִיאֵ֣ל אֲרִיאֵ֔ל קִרְיַ֖ת חָנָ֣ה דָוִ֑ד סְפ֥וּ שָׁנָ֛ה עַל־ שָׁנָ֖ה חַגִּ֥ים יִנְקֹֽפוּ׃

passages.text: And I will constrain Ariel, and there will be mourning and lamentation; she will be like an altar hearth before Me.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts speaks.
He will constrain Ariel.
Ariel is the city where David camped.
Ariel will experience mourning.
Ariel will experience lamentation.
Ariel will become like an altar hearth before the LORD.
passages.original: וַהֲצִיק֖וֹתִי לַֽאֲרִיאֵ֑ל וְהָיְתָ֤ה תַֽאֲנִיָּה֙ וַֽאֲנִיָּ֔ה וְהָ֥יְתָה לִּ֖י כַּאֲרִיאֵֽל׃

passages.text: I will camp in a circle around you; I will besiege you with towers and set up siege works against you.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Ariel, the city where David camped.
God says, “I will camp all around you.
I will surround you on every side.
I will attack you with towers.
I will build siege works against you.”
passages.original: וְחָנִ֥יתִי כַדּ֖וּר עָלָ֑יִךְ וְצַרְתִּ֤י עָלַ֙יִךְ֙ מֻצָּ֔ב וַהֲקִֽימֹתִ֥י עָלַ֖יִךְ מְצֻרֹֽת׃

passages.text: You will be brought low, you will speak from the ground, and out of the dust your words will be muffled. Your voice will be like a spirit from the ground; your speech will whisper out of the dust.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Ariel, which means Jerusalem.
God will humble you.
You will be brought low to the ground.
You will speak from the earth.
Your words will come from the dust.
Your voice will sound like a spirit from the ground.
Your speech will whisper out of the dust.
passages.original: וְשָׁפַלְתְּ֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ תְּדַבֵּ֔רִי וּמֵֽעָפָ֖ר תִּשַּׁ֣ח אִמְרָתֵ֑ךְ וְֽ֠הָיָה כְּא֤וֹב מֵאֶ֙רֶץ֙ קוֹלֵ֔ךְ וּמֵעָפָ֖ר אִמְרָתֵ֥ךְ תְּצַפְצֵֽף׃

passages.text: But your many foes will be like fine dust, the multitude of the ruthless like blowing chaff. Then suddenly, in an instant, you will be visited by the LORD of Hosts with thunder and earthquake and loud noise, with windstorm and tempest and consuming flame of fire.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts is God.
God will act with great power.
You have many enemies.
Your enemies are strong and ruthless.
God will make your many enemies like fine dust.
God will make the ruthless people like chaff blown by the wind.
This will happen suddenly.
This will happen in an instant.
God will come to you with thunder.
God will come with earthquake.
God will come with a loud noise.
God will come with a windstorm.
God will come with a tempest.
God will come with a consuming flame of fire.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֛ה כְּאָבָ֥ק דַּ֖ק הֲמ֣וֹן זָרָ֑יִךְ וּכְמֹ֤ץ עֹבֵר֙ הֲמ֣וֹן עָֽרִיצִ֔ים וְהָיָ֖ה לְפֶ֥תַע פִּתְאֹֽם׃ מֵעִ֨ם יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ תִּפָּקֵ֔ד בְּרַ֥עַם וּבְרַ֖עַשׁ וְק֣וֹל גָּד֑וֹל סוּפָה֙ וּסְעָרָ֔ה וְלַ֖הַב אֵ֥שׁ אוֹכֵלָֽה׃

passages.text: All the many nations going out to battle against Ariel— even all who war against her, laying siege and attacking her— will be like a dream, like a vision in the night, as when a hungry man dreams he is eating, then awakens still hungry; as when a thirsty man dreams he is drinking, then awakens faint and parched. So will it be for all the many nations who go to battle against Mount Zion.
passages.sermon:
Many nations will gather to fight against Ariel.
Ariel is another name for Jerusalem.
These nations will attack her.
They will surround her and lay siege to her.
They will try to harm her.
All these nations will be like a dream at night.
They will be like a vision that disappears in the darkness.
A hungry man may dream he is eating.
He wakes up and is still hungry.
A thirsty man may dream he is drinking.
He wakes up and is still weak and thirsty.
In the same way, all the nations who fight against Mount Zion will gain nothing.
Their efforts will be empty, like dreams that vanish when morning comes.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֗ה כַּֽחֲלוֹם֙ חֲז֣וֹן לַ֔יְלָה הֲמוֹן֙ כָּל־ הַגּוֹיִ֔ם הַצֹּבְאִ֖ים עַל־ אֲרִיאֵ֑ל וְכָל־ צֹבֶ֙יהָ֙ וּמְצֹ֣דָתָ֔הּ וְהַמְּצִיקִ֖ים לָֽהּ׃ וְהָיָ֡ה כַּאֲשֶׁר֩ יַחֲלֹ֨ם הָרָעֵ֜ב וְהִנֵּ֣ה אוֹכֵ֗ל וְהֵקִיץ֮ וְרֵיקָ֣ה נַפְשׁוֹ֒ וְכַאֲשֶׁ֨ר יַחֲלֹ֤ם הַצָּמֵא֙ וְהִנֵּ֣ה שֹׁתֶ֔ה וְהֵקִיץ֙ וְהִנֵּ֣ה עָיֵ֔ף וְנַפְשׁ֖וֹ שׁוֹקֵקָ֑ה כֵּ֣ן יִֽהְיֶ֗ה הֲמוֹן֙ כָּל־ הַגּוֹיִ֔ם הַצֹּבְאִ֖ים עַל־ הַ֥ר צִיּֽוֹן׃ס

passages.text: Stop and be astonished; blind yourselves and be sightless; be drunk, but not with wine; stagger, but not from strong drink.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people.
He tells them to stop and be amazed.
He tells them to look and be astonished.
He tells them to act confused and wander.
They are drunk, but not from wine.
They stagger, but not from strong drink.
passages.original: הִתְמַהְמְה֣וּ וּתְמָ֔הוּ הִשְׁתַּֽעַשְׁע֖וּ וָשֹׁ֑עוּ שָֽׁכְר֣וּ וְלֹא־ יַ֔יִן נָע֖וּ וְלֹ֥א שֵׁכָֽר׃

passages.text: For the LORD has poured out on you a spirit of deep sleep. He has shut your eyes, O prophets; He has covered your heads, O seers.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD has acted.
The LORD has poured out a spirit of deep sleep on you.
You are the people of Israel.
The LORD has shut your eyes.
You are the prophets.
The LORD has covered your heads.
You are the seers.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ נָסַ֨ךְ עֲלֵיכֶ֤ם יְהוָה֙ ר֣וּחַ תַּרְדֵּמָ֔ה וַיְעַצֵּ֖ם אֶת־ עֵֽינֵיכֶ֑ם אֶת־ הַנְּבִיאִ֛ים וְאֶת־ רָאשֵׁיכֶ֥ם הַחֹזִ֖ים כִּסָּֽה׃

passages.text: And the entire vision will be to you like the words sealed in a scroll. If it is handed to someone to read, he will say, “I cannot, because it is sealed.”
passages.sermon:
God gave a vision to the people.
This vision is like words in a sealed scroll.
No one can open the scroll.
Someone gives the scroll to a person who can read.
They say, “Please read this.”
The person answers, “I cannot.”
He says, “It is sealed.”
passages.original: וַתְּהִ֨י לָכֶ֜ם חָז֣וּת הַכֹּ֗ל כְּדִבְרֵי֮ הַסֵּ֣פֶר הֶֽחָתוּם֒ אֲשֶֽׁר־ יִתְּנ֣וּ אֹת֗וֹ אֶל־ יוֹדֵ֥עַ הַסֵּפֶר לֵאמֹ֖ר קְרָ֣א נָא־ זֶ֑ה וְאָמַר֙ לֹ֣א אוּכַ֔ל כִּ֥י חָת֖וּם הֽוּא׃

passages.text: Or if the scroll is handed to one unable to read, he will say, “I cannot read.”
passages.sermon:
A person receives a scroll.
This person cannot read.
Someone says, "Please read this."
The person answers, "I cannot read."
This shows the person does not know how to read.
The scroll remains unread.
passages.original: וְנִתַּ֣ן הַסֵּ֗פֶר עַל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹֽא־ יָדַ֥ע סֵ֛פֶר לֵאמֹ֖ר קְרָ֣א נָא־ זֶ֑ה וְאָמַ֕ר לֹ֥א יָדַ֖עְתִּי סֵֽפֶר׃ס

passages.text: Therefore the Lord said: “These people draw near to Me with their mouths and honor Me with their lips, but their hearts are far from Me. Their worship of Me is but rules taught by men.
passages.sermon:
The Lord spoke.
The Lord saw the people.
These people come close to Me with their mouths.
They honor Me with their lips.
Their hearts are far from Me.
They do not truly love Me in their hearts.
They worship Me only by following human rules.
Their fear of Me is just what people have taught them.
Their worship is not sincere.
Their worship is not from their hearts.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲדֹנָ֗י יַ֚עַן כִּ֤י נִגַּשׁ֙ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה בְּפִ֤יו וּבִשְׂפָתָיו֙ כִּבְּד֔וּנִי וְלִבּ֖וֹ רִחַ֣ק מִמֶּ֑נִּי וַתְּהִ֤י יִרְאָתָם֙ אֹתִ֔י מִצְוַ֥ת אֲנָשִׁ֖ים מְלֻמָּדָֽה׃

passages.text: Therefore I will again confound these people with wonder upon wonder. The wisdom of the wise will vanish, and the intelligence of the intelligent will be hidden.”
passages.sermon:
The Lord speaks to the people of Israel.
The Lord says He will act again.
He will do amazing and astonishing things to these people.
He will bring wonder after wonder.
The wise people will lose their wisdom.
The intelligent people will lose their understanding.
Their knowledge will disappear.
passages.original: לָכֵ֗ן הִנְנִ֥י יוֹסִ֛ף לְהַפְלִ֥יא אֶת־ הָֽעָם־ הַזֶּ֖ה הַפְלֵ֣א וָפֶ֑לֶא וְאָֽבְדָה֙ חָכְמַ֣ת חֲכָמָ֔יו וּבִינַ֥ת נְבֹנָ֖יו תִּסְתַּתָּֽר׃ס

passages.text: Woe to those who dig deep to hide their plans from the LORD. In darkness they do their works and say, “Who sees us, and who will know?”
passages.sermon:
The Lord sees all things.
Some people try to hide their plans from the Lord.
They make their plans in secret.
They do their works in darkness.
They say, “Who sees us?”
They say, “Who will know?”
But the Lord knows every secret.
The Lord sees every hidden deed.
passages.original: ה֛וֹי הַמַּעֲמִיקִ֥ים מֵֽיהוָ֖ה לַסְתִּ֣ר עֵצָ֑ה וְהָיָ֤ה בְמַחְשָׁךְ֙ מַֽעֲשֵׂיהֶ֔ם וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ מִ֥י רֹאֵ֖נוּ וּמִ֥י יוֹדְעֵֽנוּ׃

passages.text: You have turned things upside down, as if the potter were regarded as clay. Shall what is formed say to him who formed it, “He did not make me”? Can the pottery say of the potter, “He has no understanding”?
passages.sermon:
God is the Creator.
God forms people as a potter shapes clay.
You have reversed the truth.
You act as if the potter is only clay.
A created thing cannot claim, “He did not make me.”
A pot cannot say to the potter, “He has no understanding.”
passages.original: הַ֨פְכְּכֶ֔ם אִם־ כְּחֹ֥מֶר הַיֹּצֵ֖ר יֵֽחָשֵׁ֑ב כִּֽי־ יֹאמַ֨ר מַעֲשֶׂ֤ה לְעֹשֵׂ֙הוּ֙ לֹ֣א עָשָׂ֔נִי וְיֵ֛צֶר אָמַ֥ר לְיוֹצְר֖וֹ לֹ֥א הֵבִֽין׃

passages.text: In a very short time, will not Lebanon become an orchard, and the orchard seem like a forest?
passages.sermon:
God will act soon.
He will change things quickly.
Lebanon is a land known for its forests.
God will make Lebanon like a fruitful orchard.
The orchard will become like a thick forest.
This change will happen in a very short time.
passages.original: הֲלוֹא־ עוֹד֙ מְעַ֣ט מִזְעָ֔ר וְשָׁ֥ב לְבָנ֖וֹן לַכַּרְמֶ֑ל וְהַכַּרְמֶ֖ל לַיַּ֥עַר יֵחָשֵֽׁב׃

passages.text: On that day the deaf will hear the words of the scroll, and out of the deep darkness the eyes of the blind will see.
passages.sermon:
God will act on a special day.
On that day, deaf people will hear words from a scroll.
Blind people will see.
They will see even though they are in deep darkness.
God will give hearing to the deaf.
God will give sight to the blind.
passages.original: וְשָׁמְע֧וּ בַיּוֹם־ הַה֛וּא הַחֵרְשִׁ֖ים דִּבְרֵי־ סֵ֑פֶר וּמֵאֹ֣פֶל וּמֵחֹ֔שֶׁךְ עֵינֵ֥י עִוְרִ֖ים תִּרְאֶֽינָה׃

passages.text: The humble will increase their joy in the LORD, and the poor among men will rejoice in the Holy One of Israel.
passages.sermon: The humble will find more joy in the LORD.\r\nThe poor among people will rejoice in the Holy One of Israel.
passages.original: וְיָסְפ֧וּ עֲנָוִ֛ים בַּֽיהוָ֖ה שִׂמְחָ֑ה וְאֶבְיוֹנֵ֣י אָדָ֔ם בִּקְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יָגִֽילוּ׃

passages.text: For the ruthless will vanish, the mockers will disappear, and all who look for evil will be cut down— those who indict a man with a word, who ensnare the mediator at the gate, and who with false charges deprive the innocent of justice.
passages.sermon:
God will act against evil people.
Ruthless people will vanish.
Mockers will disappear.
All who look for evil will be cut down.
Some people accuse others with only a word.
Some people trap the mediator at the gate.
Some people use false charges.
These people deprive the innocent of justice.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ אָפֵ֥ס עָרִ֖יץ וְכָ֣לָה לֵ֑ץ וְנִכְרְת֖וּ כָּל־ שֹׁ֥קְדֵי אָֽוֶן׃ מַחֲטִיאֵ֤י אָדָם֙ בְּדָבָ֔ר וְלַמּוֹכִ֥יחַ בַּשַּׁ֖עַר יְקֹשׁ֑וּן וַיַּטּ֥וּ בַתֹּ֖הוּ צַדִּֽיק׃ס

passages.text: Therefore the LORD who redeemed Abraham says of the house of Jacob: “No longer will Jacob be ashamed and no more will his face grow pale.
passages.sermon:
The LORD redeemed Abraham.
The LORD speaks to the house of Jacob.
The LORD says these words.
Jacob will not be ashamed.
Jacob’s face will not grow pale.
passages.original: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־ בֵּ֣ית יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב אֲשֶׁ֥ר פָּדָ֖ה אֶת־ אַבְרָהָ֑ם לֹֽא־ עַתָּ֤ה יֵבוֹשׁ֙ יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וְלֹ֥א עַתָּ֖ה פָּנָ֥יו יֶחֱוָֽרוּ׃

passages.text: For when he sees his children around him, the work of My hands, they will honor My name, they will sanctify the Holy One of Jacob, and they will stand in awe of the God of Israel.
passages.sermon:
God redeemed Abraham and speaks to the house of Jacob.
Jacob will see his children around him.
His children are the work of God's hands.
Jacob's children will honor God's name.
They will set apart the Holy One of Jacob.
They will stand in awe of the God of Israel.
passages.original: כִּ֣י בִ֠רְאֹתוֹ יְלָדָ֞יו מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יָדַ֛י בְּקִרְבּ֖וֹ יַקְדִּ֣ישֽׁוּ שְׁמִ֑י וְהִקְדִּ֙ישׁוּ֙ אֶת־ קְד֣וֹשׁ יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וְאֶת־ אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יַעֲרִֽיצוּ׃

passages.text: Then the wayward in spirit will come to understanding, and those who grumble will accept instruction.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel.
Some people have wandered in their hearts.
These people do not understand.
God will help them understand.
Some people complain and grumble.
These people do not accept teaching.
God will teach them.
They will learn and accept instruction.
passages.original: וְיָדְע֥וּ תֹֽעֵי־ ר֖וּחַ בִּינָ֑ה וְרוֹגְנִ֖ים יִלְמְדוּ־ לֶֽקַח׃
